notes: Accept, no corrections needed. Source: the recorded arXiv e-print hash reproduces byte for byte (7828f493e9e3f26f141687381b26e379d8d5f56319351a525d4d34ed6b8bd391) and the archive contains the recorded STEForumPiRevision.tex, 1506 lines, which I read. The extraction's decision to read the source rather than the typeset PDF is recorded in `source.read`, together with the consequence that page numbers are not quoted and statement numbers are the ones the source produces; that is an honest and checkable convention, and it is what let me verify the numbering mechanically. Structure: 93 items (87 missing, 5 planned, 1 library), 3 routes (1 new roadmap, 2 source). Every missing item is routed exactly once, both source stage ids resolve, all five planned ids resolve, the new roadmap's area is a galaxy id, and check_paper.py passes. The single library item's three declarations resolve: Mathlib's ModularForm and CuspForm in NumberTheory/ModularForms/Basic.lean and SlashInvariantForm in SlashInvariantForms.lean. The new roadmap is justified. Its id is free — it appears in neither data/atlas.json nor research/blueprint/roadmaps/ nor reserved-ids.json — and a title scan of the atlas turns up no roadmap on moduli of curves or tautological rings; the two near hits, in LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles and NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties, are about semistable curves in unrelated settings. The five planned items show the imports going the right way: pure, polarized and mixed Hodge structures come from the Tau Ceti HodgeStructures roadmap, weights and purity from DWP.9, motives from MC.2, moduli representability from R09.1, local cohomology from SF.2 and pointed stable curves from the Tau Ceti StableReduction layer, none of them replanned here. Locators: the item locators are section and statement references prefixed with the arXiv version, with no pages, as the source note says. I rebuilt the paper's numbering from its twelve `\newtheorem` declarations — thm, prop, lem, cor, conj, goal, deflemma, construction, definition, example, rem and question, all sharing the `thm` counter numbered by section — and checked every statement reference in the file against it: 84 of the 85 resolve to a statement of exactly the cited kind and number. The one that does not, item 49's `Lemma 10.5`, is explicitly labelled `Lemma 10.5 of Canning–Larson` and belongs to another paper. No locator error. The single finding is confirmed. The proof of Theorem 1.5(3) opens `for even k ≥ 14' while the theorem states `for even k ≤ 14' and the proof's own next-but-one sentence uses `in all of these cases with k ≤ 14'; Conjecture 1.8, which the introduction says is open for k = 16, 18, 20, is `for even k ≤ 20'. The printed inequality is reversed, `affects: nothing' is right, and the recorded correction is the only reading that makes the proof's own appeal to the CKgP table apply. One provenance gap I did not fill: no `libraryPins` are recorded, so there is no commit against which the three library declarations were checked. I verified them against the index this lane uses and they are there, but have not invented a pin the extraction did not use. PAPER-BHATT-MATHEW-23, PAPER-WOOD-19 and PAPER-HACON-WITASZEK-23, all reviewed today, have the same gap; it looks systematic rather than accidental and may be worth a queue-level fix.
